accord_swarm.name: Accord Swarm
accord_swarm.description: Thirty boids, four names for a three-number weight vector, and the question the family never asks: which of the four, if any, would the rules put back. Three artifacts in this corpus declare an axis called `accord` and all three declare the same four words in the same order - school, orb, lane, lattice - and all three default to school. The axis names which of Reynolds' three rules the neighbourhood is obeying, so the four words are four samples of a continuous (separation, alignment, cohesion) space with no boundary drawn between them. This bench integrates the actual law - boids_aquarium's, semi-implicit Euler, fixed 1/120 s step, 240 steps = 2.000 s, seed 1987 - inside a 0.56 x 0.40 x 0.56 m wire cage on a 0.72 x 0.58 x 0.72 m stand that is identical in all twelve cells. `flock` shows where the 2.000 s left the bodies. `weights` draws one rod per rule at every boid, of length weight x 0.030 m along that rule's own direction, and draws NOTHING where the rule has no neighbour to act on - so at lane and at lattice the frame is its own flock frame to the byte, because their declared weights multiply a vector that is identically zero at all thirty boids. `recover` kicks every boid by 0.10 m/s along its own Fibonacci direction, with the mean removed so the total impulse is exactly zero, runs the same 2.000 s again, and draws the settled state as dark sites with a tether to each body. Measured on a Python replica: boids carrying at least one neighbour at the settled state are orb 30/30, school 0/30, lane 0/30, lattice 0/30. Nothing animates, nothing bakes on a worker thread, and the only draw from the seeded stream is school's cloud and lattice's drift headings.
dev_themes: one word for four regions of a continuous space
interactions: walk the accord axis at reading=weights and count the rods: thirty at orb, none at school, none at lane, none at lattice. Three of the four declared arrangements have no rule acting on them at all, and the frame says so by being identical to its own flock frame

put lane at flock beside lane at weights and look for the difference. There is none, to the byte. Then put orb at flock beside orb at weights and see the difference the rig is perfectly capable of drawing

walk the accord axis at reading=recover and read the envelopes, not the tethers: the bead is where it was, the sheet has gone from 0.016 m thick to 0.341 m, the ranks have spread from 0.258 m to 0.550 m in z, and the cloud is exactly the cloud it always was

stand at orb, reading=recover and notice that the tethers are long - mean 0.055 m against a bead whose rms radius is 0.030 m - while the bead itself has not moved. Reynolds' rules are permutation-symmetric, so no rule can promise a boid its own place back; only the shape can return

compare school at flock with school at recover: two different photographs of the same gas. The critic will call that a 75% change and it is a fact about the metric, not about the flock - recovery of a gas is a permutation, and a per-pixel comparison is not permutation-invariant
accord_swarm.capacity: SEE that `accord` names four regions of a three-number space and says nothing about which of them the rules would maintain - and that when you check, three of the four are held by nothing at all, and the fourth is held by a spring with no damping, so none of them is an attractor

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The STAND is the footprint and it is drawn before either axis is consulted: a 0.72 x 0.72 m base frame, four corner posts to y 0.58, and a 0.56 x 0.40 x 0.56 m wire cage hung at y 0.30. Boids bounce at the cage walls, so no body centre can ever leave the box; the body's own half-diagonal is 0.0395 m, which puts the widest reach at 0.320 m of a 0.36 m half-stand. Weight rods are clipped to the cage, so their reach is 0.287 m. The union AABB is therefore the STAND, 0.72 x 0.58 x 0.72, in all twelve cells and the camera never moves - which matters here more than usual, because a lane is naturally flat and an orb is naturally compact and the flock's own extent runs from 0.070 m at orb to 0.556 m at school, a factor of eight. layout=ladder stands all four accords in a row at 0.90 m pitch, about 2.7 m wide, runs four simulations instead of one, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants; no Godot was run. The box is the STAND and nothing else: the base rails span x and z +-0.36, the four posts top out at y 0.58, and the cage runs x and z +-0.28 about y 0.30. The drawn flock's own extent runs 0.059 x 0.060 x 0.070 at orb, 0.470 x 0.016 x 0.470 at lane, 0.458 x 0.252 x 0.258 at lattice and 0.514 x 0.353 x 0.556 at school - which is exactly why the stand exists and why it is drawn before the simulation runs.

dna.default: accord=school, reading=flock. school is the default because it is the default of ALL THREE members - three of three, which no other family in this corpus has managed - and because in all three it is the value that deposits nothing and leaves the shipped behaviour alone: boid_manager's _spawn_school never assigns a weight, boids_aquarium's _accord_weights falls through to a snapshot of whatever the scene authored, swarm_hive's _deposit_accord seeds a stream and returns. flock is the default because it is the family's own condition: all three members render exactly this, bodies where the law left them, with no rig holding anything still and no question asked. NOTE WHAT THIS COSTS: the default cell is the plainest tile in the sheet, an irregular cloud in a box - which would normally be a bad place to solve framing, except that framing here is set by the stand and the stand is identical in every variant, so the camera distance is the same whichever cell is measured.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, which of Reynolds' three rules each one names, and the three numbers each one sets. THE FAMILY FIRST, and it is a census before it is an argument: three artifacts declare an axis called `accord` and all three declare the SAME FOUR WORDS IN THE SAME ORDER - school | orb | lane | lattice - and all three ship `school` as the default. Three members, one vocabulary, one order, one default: three of three, which is the cleanest agreement any family in this corpus has produced. It is also three separate scenes carrying three separate scripts on three separate roots - boid_manager.tscn -> boid_manager.gd, boids_aquarium.tscn -> boids_aquarium.gd, swarm_hive.tscn -> swarm_hive.gd - so this is not the one-scene-many-names pattern; it is one name, three scenes, checked.

THE WEIGHTS, character for character out of the three files (separation / alignment / cohesion):
            boid_manager      boids_aquarium     swarm_hive
  school    1.5 / 1.0 / 1.0   1.5 / 1.0 / 1.0    2.0 / 1.0 / 1.0
  orb       0.4 / 0.6 / 4.5   0.0 / 0.0 / 4.5    0.4 / 0.6 / 4.5
  lane      0.9 / 4.5 / 0.6   0.0 / 4.5 / 0.5    0.9 / 4.5 / 0.6
  lattice   4.5 / 0.0 / 0.0   4.5 / 0.0 / 0.0    4.5 / 0.0 / 0.0
`lattice` is UNANIMOUS. `orb` and `lane` split two against one and `school` splits the other way, and THE SPLIT IS NOT A TYPO: boids_aquarium's own comments record running the majority's numbers through its own update loop and watching them destroy the shape - "sep 0.30 -> 0.0 ... the bead fills the whole tank (0.88 m extent) within 1.1 s", "sep 0.8 -> 0.0 ... separation thickens the slab from 0.120 m to 0.201 m by 1.1 s and 0.487 m by 2.5 s", "align 0.5 -> 0.0 ... alignment acts as pure drag and collapses the bead to 0.076 m by 3 s". The two members that agree are the two that never ran the test: both deposit their arrangement and cap the speed so that nothing has time to move. This bench uses boids_aquarium's triples, and the reason is in `declines`.

THE THING THE CODE SAYS THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT, and it is the finding. THE BRIEF ASKED WHETHER `lattice` IS EMERGENT OR IMPOSED. It is imposed, in all three members, and the code says so three separate ways. (1) All three DEPOSIT it - _spawn_lattice and _deposit_lattice write a regular grid arithmetically, and there is no branch anywhere in this family where a lattice arises from the rules. (2) Separation alone cannot pick one out: in all three laws separation is purely repulsive, monotone decreasing with distance and zero past a cutoff, so it has no finite equilibrium spacing at all - EVERY arrangement past the cutoff is a fixed point, the fixed-point set is a continuum, and a lattice is one arbitrary member of it. (3) Both members that comment on it say it outright. swarm_hive: "a regular grid whose spacing is WIDER than separation_radius, so the rule is satisfied everywhere". boids_aquarium: "At 0.20 m spacing and perception 0.15 nobody has a neighbour, so the deposit is a fixed point TRIVIALLY."

AND THE SAME IS TRUE OF `lane`, WHICH IS THE PART NOBODY HAD WRITTEN DOWN. boids_aquarium's own note says "at 0.168 m column spacing nothing is inside perception 0.15, so no rule acts on the sheet at all and it simply slides". So TWO of the four declared arrangements are held by nothing whatsoever, and their declared weights - 4.5, the heaviest number in the family - multiply a vector that is identically zero at every boid.

THE RULE THAT COULD HAVE HELD THEM, and this is the sharpest thing in the pass. Of Reynolds' three, separation (sum of d/|d|^2) and cohesion (mean p - p) depend on POSITION only and are conservative: they store energy and never remove it. Alignment (mean v - v) depends on VELOCITY and is the family's ONLY dissipative term - boids_aquarium calls it exactly that, "alignment acts as pure drag", in the comment explaining why it had to switch alignment off to keep the bead. So `lane` is the one value that names the only rule capable of settling anything, and at lane's own spacing that rule never fires once. And `orb`'s repair - setting alignment to 0 so the bead would stand for the camera - is exactly what removed the last damping from the system.

WHICH MAKES THE THESIS SHARPER THAN THE BRIEF'S. The brief expected some accords to be STABLE ATTRACTORS and others TRANSIENT. NOTHING HERE IS AN ATTRACTOR, because an attractor needs a sink and this family has none: the only places energy can leave are the speed clamp and the wall bounce, and at `orb` neither fires (settled speeds reach 0.083 m/s and the kick takes them to 0.183 m/s against a 0.28 m/s cap). `orb` is a CENTRE - thirty independent closed ellipses about a centroid that cannot move - so a disturbed bead BREATHES FOREVER. Measured on the replica at 0.2 s intervals through the recovery window, its rms radius runs 1.222, 1.872, 2.407, 2.747, 2.886, 2.818, 2.549, 2.074, 1.441, 1.007 of its settled value. It returns infinitely often and settles never. The other three do not even have that.

ACCORD, four values. The family's own four, in the family's own order.

  school  - sep 1.5 / ali 1.0 / coh 1.0, perception 0.112 m. TWO MEMBERS AGREE (boid_manager's Boid.gd defaults and boids_aquarium's own .tscn); swarm_hive says 2.0 / 1.0 / 1.0. In all three it is the value that deposits NOTHING and leaves the shipped behaviour alone. Here: thirty boids through the middle 60% of the cage at half the speed cap. IT IS NOT A FLOCK. With separation unnormalised the equilibrium spacing of these weights is metres wide, far outside any tank, so the cloud expands until it meets glass and then bounces - and at 2.000 s, 0 of 30 boids still have a neighbour. Settled extent 0.514 x 0.353 x 0.556 m in a 0.56 x 0.40 x 0.56 m cage: the shape of `school` is the shape of the box. That is the shipped default photographed honestly, and this repo already carries a plan file named boids_aquarium_never_flocks.

  orb     - sep 0.0 / ali 0.0 / coh 4.5, perception 0.112 m. Cohesion alone, and the aquarium's triple rather than the majority's 0.4 / 0.6 / 4.5 for the measured reason above. A solid bead: thirty Fibonacci directions, radius R * t^(1/3) so the interior fills evenly, orbital speed r * sqrt(coh) about each boid's own axis, net momentum subtracted. Max pair distance 0.078 m against perception 0.112, so EVERY BOID SEES EVERY OTHER - 870 ordered pairs, 30 of 30 boids carrying a neighbour. THE ONLY VALUE IN THE SHEET WHERE ANY RULE ACTS. Settled extent 0.059 x 0.060 x 0.070 m; rms radius 0.0297 m.

  lane    - sep 0.0 / ali 4.5 / coh 0.5, perception 0.084 m. Alignment alone. A 0.470 x 0.016 x 0.470 m sheet, six columns by five rows by three layers, every velocity +X at 0.015 m/s so the alignment term is exactly zero by construction. THE CLOSEST PAIR IS 0.0944 m APART AGAINST A 0.084 m PERCEPTION RADIUS - a 12.4% margin - and because every velocity is identical that spacing can never change. No rule acts, at any time, at any seed. The sheet translates 0.030 m in 2.000 s and that is the entire history. 0 of 30 boids have a neighbour.

  lattice - sep 4.5 / ali 0.0 / coh 0.0, perception 0.084 m. Separation alone, and the one triple all three members agree on to the character. A 5 x 3 x 2 grid spanning 0.448 x 0.240 x 0.246 m, spacing 0.112 / 0.120 / 0.246 m, each boid given a 0.004 m/s drift so the ranks point thirty different ways rather than all one way. The closest spacing is 0.112 m; two boids drifting straight at each other close at most 2 x 0.004 x 2.000 = 0.016 m over the window, so nothing can come nearer than 0.096 m against a 0.084 m radius. A 14% margin that is ARITHMETIC AND NOT LUCK, which is what makes the null below registrable. 0 of 30 boids have a neighbour.

READING, three values, and it is THIS SYNTHESIS'S OWN AXIS. No member declares anything like it: boid_manager's second export is `emissive` (a look flag), boids_aquarium's other exports are quantities and colours, swarm_hive declined a second axis outright. `reading` is therefore SYNTHESIS-INTRODUCED, and what it does is ask the same settled flock three different questions.

  flock   - the thirty bodies where 2.000 s of the law left them, each oriented to its own velocity, and nothing else. THE FAMILY'S CONDITION, DRAWN: a reader cannot tell from this frame alone whether an arrangement is held or merely left. Weights in force: whichever the accord declares - 1.5/1.0/1.0, 0.0/0.0/4.5, 0.0/4.5/0.5, 4.5/0.0/0.0.

  weights - the same frame plus, at every boid, one rod per rule: length = that rule's declared weight x 0.030 m, direction = that rule's own accumulated term, and NOTHING WHERE THE TERM IS ZERO. So the rod is the declaration and its presence is whether the declaration reaches anything. Rod lengths as declared: separation 0.045 m at school and 0.135 m at lattice; alignment 0.030 m at school and 0.135 m at lane; cohesion 0.030 m at school, 0.015 m at lane and 0.135 m at orb. RODS ACTUALLY DRAWN, measured on the replica: orb 30, school 0, lane 0, lattice 0. ISOLATES THE QUESTION 'WHAT IS ACTING', AND ANSWERS IT WITH AN UNCHANGED FRAME THREE TIMES OUT OF FOUR.

  recover - the load test, and it carries the thesis. Every boid takes an impulse of exactly 0.10 m/s along its own Fibonacci direction, with the mean of the thirty directions subtracted so the total impulse is exactly zero and no accord can be pushed off centre; then the same 2.000 s runs again. The settled state is drawn as dark 0.024 m site cubes, the new state as the lit bodies, and a 0.009 m tether joins each site to its body. No dice anywhere in the disturbance: every accord receives the identical thirty vectors in the identical order. MEASURED - settled extent -> extent 2.000 s after the kick: orb 0.059 x 0.060 x 0.070 -> 0.060 x 0.067 x 0.082; lane 0.470 x 0.016 x 0.470 -> 0.538 x 0.341 x 0.558 (THE SHEET'S THICKNESS, WHICH IS ITS WHOLE IDENTITY, GOES UP BY A FACTOR OF TWENTY-ONE); lattice 0.458 x 0.252 x 0.258 -> 0.549 x 0.377 x 0.550; school 0.514 x 0.353 x 0.556 -> 0.518 x 0.388 x 0.527. Tether means 0.055 / 0.119 / 0.180 / 0.195 m at orb / lane / lattice / school.

WHAT THE TETHERS DO NOT MEASURE, and it matters. Reynolds' rules are permutation-symmetric: no rule anywhere in this family distinguishes boid 7 from boid 19, so NO RULE CAN PROMISE ANY BOID ITS OWN PLACE BACK. What can come back is the SHAPE. That is why orb's tethers are long - mean 0.055 m against a bead whose rms radius is 0.030 m, so the boids have completely reshuffled - while the bead itself is where it was. Read the envelope, not the tether. And `school` is the case that makes the point in the other direction: its envelope is unchanged to within 1%, its pixels change by about 75%, and the critic can only see the pixels, because recovery of a gas is a permutation and a per-pixel metric is not permutation-invariant.

THE COLOUR CHECK, AND THE BRIEF'S PRIOR CORRECTED. The brief warned that boids_aquarium's `accord` was involved in the colour-only finding. What the source and the report actually say is narrower and the opposite way round. boids_aquarium's _paint_boids walks the SAME seeded palette in all four accord values, under its own rule - "Colour is not the axis: the same seeded palette walk in all four values, so a reviewer comparing tiles is comparing SHAPE" - and doc/reports/dna_bite_swarm.json lists its colour_only array as EMPTY. What is true is that artifact_dna_critic.focus_rgb's docstring records the luminance-versus-per-channel ratio being calibrated "across both swarm artifacts", and cites AntColonyV2's anchorage - 5.52% in luminance against 12.06% per channel - as the case that motivated the rescue. So `accord` was part of the CALIBRATION SAMPLE, not one of the twins. This bench goes further than its source anyway: every body in every cell is one colour, C_BODY, at every accord, so a colour-only difference is not constructible on this sheet at all. The three rod colours differ in Rec.709 luminance by design (0.636 / 0.748 / 0.558) and, decisively, in LENGTH, since length is the declared weight - and in practice only one of the three, cohesion, is ever drawn.

THE SEED, SAID PLAINLY. One RandomNumberGenerator per build, seeded 1987 (Reynolds, "Flocks, Herds and Schools of Fishes", which is boids_aquarium's own DEPOSIT_SEED). The global RNG is never touched. It is drawn from in exactly two places: school's cloud (positions and headings) and lattice's drift headings. orb, lane, the stage, the disturbance and the entire law are arithmetic. THE REPLICA'S GENERATOR IS NOT GODOT'S - an LCG, not PCG32 - so the replica's school cloud is a different sample of the same distribution. Every claim above that depends on a specific draw is flagged as such; every claim that matters is a bound over all draws.

THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: `accord` names four regions of a three-number space and says nothing about which of them the rules would maintain - and when you check, three of the four are maintained by nothing at all, because their own declared spacing puts every boid outside every other's perception, and the fourth is maintained by a spring with no damping. THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair: this bench chose ONE member's law and ONE member's radii, and a reader can say the vacuity is an artifact of boids_aquarium's single small perception radius rather than a fact about the family. The answer is that this is precisely the finding - the three members disagree about WHO COUNTS AS A NEIGHBOUR (one radius here, two in boid_manager, three in swarm_hive, where cohesion_radius 2.5 m around a 0.5 m hive means everybody always sees everybody) - and that this disagreement, which reads like a tuning detail, decides whether Reynolds' rules act at all. The cell where holding the thesis costs something is `lane` at `weights`, where a bench that believes the rule is doing nothing is obliged to publish a frame identical to its own `flock` frame: a tile that looks like a broken capture and is the argument.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: orb against lattice, in the recover reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
Rasterised BEFORE ANY CAPTURE in the critic's own currency. The whole artifact was rebuilt in Python from the same constants - same deposits, same terms, same semi-implicit Euler at 1/120 s for 240 + 240 steps, same stage - then projected through capture_config_sweep's camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, framing 0.60 on the union AABB of all twelve variants, which is the STAND at 0.72 x 0.58 x 0.72 and therefore identical in every cell), z-buffered with the default rig's key at (-42, -35) energy 1.25, fill at (-20, 130) energy 0.45 and ambient (0.62, 0.65, 0.72) at 0.55, FILMIC tonemapped, sRGB out - then run through artifact_dna_critic's pipeline: subject bbox from pixel (3,3), crop to the union of the two frames' boxes, grey, box-average to 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5 percent.

THE SUBJECT BOX IS THE SAME IN ALL TWELVE CELLS - 48.6 percent of frame - because the subject is the stand. Ink coverage per cell, flock / weights / recover: orb 10.88 / 11.25 / 10.92 percent, school 13.22 / 13.22 / 15.37, lane 13.48 / 13.48 / 15.47, lattice 13.10 / 13.10 / 14.79.

THE CONTEXT IS THE `recover` READING AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT. All six pairs, focus percent: orb-lattice 71.64, orb-lane 74.35, lane-lattice 75.14, school-orb 75.21, school-lane 75.81, school-lattice 75.82.

WHY THAT PAIR. orb is the only accord whose flock is a compact knot - 0.082 m across against about 0.55 m for the other three after the kick - so it puts the least ink on the frame (10.92 percent against 14.79) and the union of the two tiles' ink is the smallest of the six pairs. lattice is the least spread of the remaining three. Every other pair puts two box-filling flocks against each other.

AND NOW THE PART THAT MAKES THIS PREDICTION WORTH REGISTERING: THE SHEET IS SATURATED, SO THE RANKING IS WEAK EVIDENCE AND THAT IS SAID IN ADVANCE. Every pair changes at least 20 percent of the crop while the hottest-5-percent window is 1280 pixels, so the window fills entirely with full-contrast body-against-background pixels in all six cases and the six numbers land within 4.2 points of each other - 71.64 to 75.82, on a base near 74. In the `flock` reading the top two are separated by 0.06 of a point (orb-lattice 71.69, school-orb 71.75), which is A TIE AND IS DECLARED AS ONE HERE rather than reported afterwards as a single pair. `recover` was chosen as the context precisely because it has the clearest gap of the three, 2.7 points, and even that is small.

THE DIRECTION OF THE EXPECTED ERROR IS THE OPPOSITE OF THIS CORPUS'S USUAL. Every prior prediction here UNDER-read by 1.5x to 6.7x because the replica was a simplification of the artifact. This one is a full geometric replica - every box Godot will draw is drawn here - so the residual differences are shading only: no shadows (which would ADD difference, since four different flocks cast four different patterns onto the base frame), no AO, and no antialiasing (which softens edges but not the interior pixels the hottest 5 percent selects). So 71.6 is a CENTRE, not a floor, and the sweep is expected within about 10 points either way. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK UNDER 40 PERCENT ON ANY PAIR IN THIS READING, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py - a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles; (b) _rejects.json - both axes are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=12, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 the 4 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail of the LATER axis and `reading` collapses to [flock, weights], which deletes this reading entirely.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND IT IS THE THESIS, not a spare check. `weights` draws a rod only where the rule it names has a neighbour to act on. In lane's deposit the closest pair is 0.0944 m apart against a perception radius of 0.084 m, and every velocity is exactly (0.015, 0, 0), so no relative position ever changes and no boid ever acquires a neighbour - at any seed, at any step count. All three of lane's declared weights, including the 4.5 on alignment, multiply a vector that is identically zero at all thirty boids, so no rod is constructed, no SurfaceTool commits, and the two frames are the same mesh set under the same materials. Predicted 0.000 percent, confirmed at 0.000 on the replica; anything above 0.5 percent is render noise, and anything above 2 percent means a rod was drawn where no rule acts.

The same null, second value, and registered separately because it is the one the whole family agrees on. lattice's triple - 4.5 / 0.0 / 0.0 - is declared identically by all three members and is the largest single weight in the family. Rank spacing is 0.112 m against a perception radius of 0.084 m; the 0.004 m/s drift can close a pair by at most 2 x 0.004 x 2.000 = 0.016 m over the window, so the nearest any two boids can come is 0.096 m - a 14 percent margin that holds for EVERY possible set of drift headings, which is what makes this null independent of Godot's RNG differing from the replica's. The heaviest declared weight in the corpus's most agreed-on value draws nothing. If this one comes back non-zero while lane's holds, the fault is in the drift bound and not in the argument.

A BOUND, NOT AN IDENTITY, AND IT IS THE ONE IN THIS SET THAT CAN BREAK - registered anyway, because a prediction that cannot be wrong is worth nothing. school's cloud is the only arrangement here drawn from the RNG, and Godot's PCG32 will not reproduce the replica's LCG sample, so the exact encounters differ. What does not differ is the regime: with these weights the equilibrium spacing is far wider than the cage, so the cloud expands to fill the box, and the expected neighbour count per boid at a 0.112 m radius in a 0.176 m^3 volume is 29 x 0.00588 / 0.176 = 0.97, which by Poisson leaves roughly a third of frames with a single chance encounter. Across five different seeds the replica measured 0, 0, 2, 2, 2 boids carrying a neighbour at exactly 2.000 s. Two boids drawing at most six rods of 0.045 / 0.030 / 0.030 m at 0.010 m section is about 0.0018 m^2 of a 0.5 m^2 crop = 0.36 percent of pixels changed against a 5 percent window, so the focus number cannot exceed about 0.36/5 x 75 = 5.4 percent even in the worst case and lands near zero in the common one. Registered under 4. IF IT COMES BACK ABOVE 6 PERCENT the finding is that these weights DO flock at this scale and the note's account of school is wrong - which would be the best thing this pass could produce.

dna.designed_nulls_why: THREE NULLS, ONE FACT. `weights` is a rig that draws the declaration only where the declaration reaches something, so a frame identical to its own `flock` frame is the rig REPORTING THAT NOTHING ACTS. That report is unambiguous only because the sheet also contains the cell where the rig plainly does draw: orb at `weights` differs from orb at `flock` by 10.22 percent on the replica - thirty cohesion rods of 0.135 m each, long enough to pass through the bead and out the far side, which is the only way a rod pointing at the centre of a solid ball is visible at all. One cell proves the rig works; three cells prove there was nothing to draw. THE TEMPTING FOURTH IS NOT A NULL AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED: orb at `flock` against orb at `recover` measures 6.01 percent, which looks like a stable attractor returning and is nothing of the kind - the bead's rms radius passes through 2.886x of its settled value at 0.96 s and is back at 1.007x at 2.000 s. It is a PHASE, not a decay, and the recovery window was set equal to the settle window on principle rather than chosen to flatter it. If any of the three zeros comes back above 2 percent, nothing else in this sheet can be believed.
dna.kin: The three sources are the kin and the relation is unusually direct, because this bench shares their word, their four rungs, their default and their law rather than inventing any of it. boid_manager is a 20 x 10 x 20 m room of a hundred needles the player walks inside and pushes with a controller; its truth line is that coordination is not agreement, it is geometry, and its accord deposits four arrangements and caps the speed so they stand. boids_aquarium is a 1 m glass tank of thirty with three VR sliders; its truth line is that the boundary of the tank is the only rule that is truly external, and it is the ONE member that ran its own deposits through its own update loop and published what happened - which is why this bench takes its law and its triples. swarm_hive is a 0.5 m hazard that releases twenty stinging motes at the player; its truth line is that three rules and the swarm organizes itself, and its accord block records declining a second axis on the grounds that a weak second axis earns a faint verdict that gets misread as a fact about the design. A room holding this bench beside boids_aquarium is saying the same sentence twice about a tank; a room holding it beside swarm_hive is saying the sentence and then asking whether the rules would put it back. ON THE VALUE SIDE this is the corpus's most agreed-on shared vocabulary - three artifacts, one word, four rungs, one order, one default, and one triple (lattice, 4.5 / 0.0 / 0.0) identical to the character in all three - which is exactly the condition under which a family is supposed to MEASURE ALIKE, and the reported bites are boid_manager 14.4 percent and boids_aquarium 8.6 percent.
declines: THE BRIEF'S ARGUMENT, corrected from the code, and it is the biggest change. The brief expected some accords to be STABLE ATTRACTORS the flock returns to and others to be TRANSIENT, with lattice the imposed one. The code says lattice is imposed - three ways over, see `note` - but it also says NONE of the four is an attractor, because there is no dissipation anywhere in this family for an attractor to be built out of. Separation and cohesion are position-only and conservative; alignment is the only velocity-dependent term, and boids_aquarium switched it off at `orb` precisely because it was, in its own words, pure drag. So the split is not attractor versus transient, it is CENTRE versus NOTHING AT ALL: orb breathes forever, and school, lane and lattice have no rule acting on them whatsoever.

THE MAJORITY'S TRIPLES FOR `orb` AND `lane`, declined in favour of the minority's, and this is the one place this bench overrules two members out of three. boid_manager and swarm_hive both declare orb 0.4 / 0.6 / 4.5 and lane 0.9 / 4.5 / 0.6, identically. boids_aquarium declares 0.0 / 0.0 / 4.5 and 0.0 / 4.5 / 0.5 and states in its own comments that it MEASURED the other numbers against its own loop first: separation 0.30 blows the bead to 0.88 m inside 1.1 s, alignment 0.5 collapses it to 0.076 m by 3 s, separation 0.8 thickens the lane slab from 0.120 m to 0.487 m by 2.5 s. Since this bench adopts the aquarium's LAW - one perception radius, unnormalised separation summing d/|d|^2 - it must adopt the triples that were measured against that law; pairing the majority's weights with the minority's force expression would reproduce the failure the aquarium documented and then report it as a finding. THE MAJORITY IS NOT WRONG UNDER ITS OWN LAW; it is untested under it, because both members deposit and cap the speed so nothing has time to move.

THE OTHER TWO LAWS, and this is a real loss rather than a tidy one. boid_manager normalises every term to max_speed, subtracts the current velocity and limits the result to max_force, and uses TWO radii (perception_radius for align and cohere, avoid_radius for separate). swarm_hive normalises each term to a unit vector times its weight and uses THREE radii - separation 0.5 m, alignment 1.5 m, cohesion 2.5 m around a 0.5 m hive, which means everybody always sees everybody and no arrangement can ever fall out of range. Under swarm_hive's radii the vacuity finding would not appear at all. That is not a reason to hide it: the family disagrees about who counts as a neighbour, and the disagreement decides whether the rules act. One law per bench, the choice declared, and the alternative recorded here rather than smoothed over.

`emissive` from boid_manager as a third axis. It is a real export and it bites - flat magenta albedo against a glow - but what it decides is what the boids LOOK like, not what the flock argues, and a sheet sweeping it beside `accord` would be answering two questions and able to attribute neither. It is also the key curation_station hands every curated artifact, so it belongs to the housing vocabulary rather than to this one.

A POPULATION AXIS. boid_manager ships 100, its script says 50, boids_aquarium says 30, swarm_hive caps at 20, and boids_aquarium's own sweep already crossed accord with boid_count at 10 and 105 - so the family has a live second dimension. It is declined here for a stated reason: at thirty boids the expected neighbour count at school's radius is 0.97, so population is not a look knob, it is the thing that decides whether the vacuity finding is true. An axis that can silently repair the argument does not belong in the same sheet as the argument. It is the honest third axis and the first thing to add if this bench ever needs one.

THE AQUARIUM'S VERTICAL NEEDLES, flagged rather than copied. boids_aquarium's _update_multimesh builds the transform with looking_at and then rotates the basis by -PI/2 about its own x, which puts the mesh's long axis along the UP vector rather than along the heading - its own comment says so, and says the lane sheet's 0.12 m thickness is 0.040 m of layer spread plus an 0.080 m mark STANDING VERTICAL. This bench lays the long axis along the heading, which is what a reader will assume a boid does. The consequence is that lane's sheet is 0.016 + 0.026 = 0.042 m thick here where the aquarium's is 0.120 m, and that difference is a fact about the two meshes rather than about the two flocks.

A TIME AXIS, and every rate, duration and phase in it. The evidence for this axis is one PNG per variant and a rate is invisible to a still - which cost `info_board` six identical tiles. It would also have been the easy way out here: the whole difference between `orb` and the rest is visible in a still precisely because the deposits stand. What IS a time claim - the bead breathing to 2.886x at 0.96 s and back to 1.007x at 2.000 s - is written into the note as a measured trajectory rather than declared as a rung, because no still can carry it.

NORMALISING THE RECOVERY WINDOW TO THE BEAD'S BREATHING PERIOD. It was considered and it is exactly the wrong move: choosing the window so that the bead comes back is choosing the answer. The window is 2.000 s because the settle window is 2.000 s - a disturbance gets the same time the deposit got - and the fact that this lands orb at 1.007x of its settled rms is a coincidence of phase, recorded as such in `designed_nulls_why` rather than presented as recovery.

A LARGER FLOCK OR A LARGER MARK. Thirty bodies of 0.070 x 0.026 m already put 10.9 to 15.5 percent ink on the frame, and the replica shows every accord pair changing more than 20 percent of the crop against a 5 percent measurement window - the sheet is SATURATED, and all six pairs in a reading land within 4.2 points of each other. More ink buys nothing and costs the ranking. The mark is not made smaller either: that is the exact fault boids_aquarium had to repair, three declared values rendering as one picture at 176 pixels of ink.

GODOT'S RNG BEING REPRODUCED IN THE REPLICA. It is not, and cannot be from Python without reimplementing PCG32, so the replica's school cloud and lattice drift headings are a different sample of the same distributions. Every load-bearing claim is therefore written as a bound over ALL draws - lane has no RNG at all, lattice's null is a worst-case closure argument, and orb, the stage and the disturbance are pure arithmetic - and the one claim that depends on a specific sample, school's rod count, is registered as a bound with a stated failure mode rather than as an identity.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=12 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS THE THESIS. `accord` is declared first and is never trimmed; `reading` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the default --max=9 the 4 x 3 sheet renders as 4 x 2 - flock and weights only - which is the cruellest possible truncation here, because it KEEPS all three designed nulls and DELETES the reading that explains them. The result is eight tiles in which two pairs are byte-identical, no prediction can be checked, and the sheet looks finished. BUILD COST: each cell runs 240 integration steps at flock and at weights and 480 at recover, over thirty boids at O(n^2), so the whole sheet is about 4.3 million pair evaluations spread over twelve synchronous builds. Nothing awaits, nothing defers, nothing waits for convergence, and the worst single cell is 432 000 pair evaluations - this artifact is not in the named headless hang class and does not share its mechanism.
